common_name: Wallich's Sweet Box (Tall Himalayan Fragrant Sarcococca)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; Wallich's sweet box is taller and more loosely arching than the commonly grown S. confusa or S. hookeriana and is best sited in a mild, maritime-influenced climate.

directions: Site in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, sheltered from cold, drying winds and hard freezes. Sarcococca wallichii is a loosely clumping Himalayan species distinguished from its better-known relatives by a notably taller, more arching habit and larger, glossy lance-shaped leaves reaching up to four inches long, giving it a bolder, more architectural presence than the low, spreading sweet box species usually grown as groundcover. Small, creamy-white flowers open in the depths of winter and carry the same intensely sweet, honeyed fragrance typical of the genus, perfuming the surrounding air on mild days before giving way to black fruit. Because it is less cold-hardy than S. confusa or S. hookeriana, reserve it for the milder end of its range or a protected microclimate, water during dry spells while establishing, and prune only to remove damaged or overly leggy stems.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society) - Sarcococca
